evidence.notes: All three builds keep the Reporting API contract (no src/api or src/mock edits, GET-only page loads, original selectors preserved; region-row is generated dynamically in X and Z). All converge on a similar analytics-first IA: interactive KPI switch tiles, a hand-built SVG trend with prior-period overlay and anomaly markers, and a drillable region/store/category comparison with trend-bucket drill-down. X is the most complete: explicit no-sales empty state, inline viewer lock on Export, a confirmation dialog with receipt, and an anomaly 'Investigate' that scopes filters, metric and period. On mobile it caps the anomaly list so the trend stays primary; its main flaws are a detail-page contrast issue and a clipped column at 768. Z is close behind, with better heading semantics and focus treatment, but shows misleading $0/0.0% tiles in the empty scenario, reveals the viewer restriction only after the panel opens, and runs long on mobile. Y has the richest drill panel and proactive stale-data detection, but trails on presentation: no h1, an awkward 768 filter layout, a horizontally scrolling mobile table, unicode-glyph icons and zero-valued empty tiles.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: The page flows from KPI switch tiles to a full-width trend, then comparison and anomalies side by side. Selecting a trend bucket scopes the comparison ('Showing Sep 28 only · Back to full range').
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: Analytics-first. Anomalies offer Show on trend and Filter to scope or Open store, and fleet-wide category and segment signals are labelled when a store or region is filtered. The store category links back to a store+category-filtered overview.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: src/api and src/mock are untouched and loads are GET-only. region-row is kept via rowTestId={`${dimension}-row`} (grep false negative), the export-button testid stays on the trigger, and the other selectors are preserved.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: Covers skeleton loading, error with retry, partial banner and pre-export rejection warning, STALE_VERSION reload, and a receipt with server-applied filters. The empty scenario shows '$0 / 0.0% vs 0.0%' tiles, and store detail wrongly attributes missing comparison to 'opened Mar 22, 2014'. The viewer only learns export is unavailable after opening the panel.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No overflow. Filters collapse at 375 and the comparison becomes stacked cards at ≤820px. The anomaly list is uncapped (8 full items), making mobile pages long, and there is large whitespace under the comparison at 1440.
scorer_rationale.accessibility: Has a skip link, h1 per page, a box-shadow focus ring with forced-colors outline fallback (focusVisible on all 30 stops at 375), and a chart keyboard nav with describedby instructions and a data table. Export panel focus management and Escape work, and axe is clean.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Clean, restrained, consistent icon set. The anomaly column is long and uneven against the comparison card.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Compact (3.6k LOC) with clear lib split (useApi with seq guard, filters.ts, metrics.ts, describeFilters). The 'Quarter to date' preset is hard-wired to defaultRange.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: The export panel lists the exact slice and format before 'Start CSV export', disables during flight, polls, and shows a receipt with rowCount, snapshot, server-applied filters and download. It gives an explicit partial-data rejection warning.

overfitting.dominant_ia: KPI switch + full-width trend + comparison/anomaly split with bucket-scoped breakdown
justified_patterns: prior-period overlay with metric-matched anomaly rules

strengths: Proper heading structure and consistent focus ring
Comparison scoped to the selected trend bucket
Receipt shows filters as applied by the server
Clean mobile card recomposition of the comparison
defects: Store detail misattributes missing prior data to the opening date
Viewer restriction is hidden until the export panel is opened
'Quarter to date' preset hard-mapped to defaultRange
